steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Once you use Claude every day, you'll wonder "How much can I use?" and "What if it suddenly stops?" Today you'll learn about plans and usage limits, and how to check your own usage.

  • Time: 10 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 7
You won't create or edit any files today. Just read, click and check.

steps.title: Plans at a glance
steps.html:
FreeChat only. No Claude Code
Pro$20/month ($17/month billed yearly). Includes Claude Code. Enough for this course
Max$100/month. 5× Pro usage
Ultra$200/month. For heavy users

Prices in US dollars, before tax. They can vary by country and change over time, so check claude.com/pricing for exact amounts.

check.q: Do you know which plan you're on?

steps.title: Find out your plan
steps.html:
• Click your name at the bottom left of the Claude app (or claude.ai). It usually shows your plan name (e.g. Pro plan).
  • If you used the Code tab in Desktop 1, you're already on a paid plan. Free can't use the Code tab.

steps.title: There are two usage limits
steps.html:
Even paid plans aren't unlimited. There are two limits.

5-hour limitRefills every 5 hours, counting from when you send your first message
Weekly limitRefills every week at a fixed day and time set for your account
Chat and Claude Code share the same limits. Phone chats, claude.ai and the desktop Code tab all count together.

Limits differ by plan and may change over time.

steps.title: Check your usage
steps.html:
1. Open the Claude app → Code tab.
  2. Click the small circle (usage ring) at the right of the row under the typing box.

It shows what % of Current session (5-hour limit) and Weekly you've used, and when each refills.
steps.alt: Clicking the usage ring under the typing box to see 5-hour and weekly usage

check.q: Can you see your usage % and when it refills?

steps.title: If you can't see the usage ring
steps.html:
• You can see the same thing in a web browser at claude.ai/settings/usage (claude.ai → Settings → Usage).
  • Older app versions may not have the ring. Try updating the app.

choices.label: I saw it on the web, next

steps.title: Quick quiz!
steps.html: Current session shows 90% and "Resets in 2 hr". You were about to hand over a big cleanup job. What should you do?

choices.label: Save the big job for after the reset; do small things now
Make another account with no limit

steps.title: Hmm, we wouldn't recommend that
steps.html: A new account has the same limits, and you'd have to start your chats and settings over. Splitting your work around the reset time is simplest. If you often run short, then consider a bigger plan.

steps.title: Correct! And tips to use less
steps.html:
Planning around the reset time is best. Day to day, these habits use less of your limit:

  • New job, new chat (Desktop 3): longer chats mean more to read each time, so they use more.
  • Be specific: "by date, as a table" instead of just "organize it" means fewer do-overs.
  • Plan big jobs first (Desktop 5): fixing the plan before running it avoids wasted work.
  • Share only what's needed: attaching many big files or pictures uses more.

steps.title: What happens when you hit the limit?
steps.html:
• Claude pauses and tells you when you can use it again.
  • Your work and chats are kept. After it refills, open the same chat and say "carry on".
  • If you often run short, then consider a bigger plan (Max, etc.). There's no need to start with an expensive one.
Handle payments and plan changes yourself, checking the amount. Don't ask Claude to pay for you.

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop basics complete!
steps.html:
You've finished all 8 desktop practices. Great work!

1–2Install and first task; read changes and edit
3–4New or continued chats; organize several files
5–6Permission modes; undo mistakes
7–8Show it pictures; plans and usage

Remember from today

  1. Check usage with the usage ring under the typing box (or claude.ai/settings/usage).
  2. There are 5-hour and weekly limits, shared by chat and Code. Split big jobs around the reset time.

What's next?

You have the basics now. The next course covers real work like spreadsheet (CSV) cleanup, document summaries and report drafts. Check your progress in All courses beside the page.
